papers.title: The Effects of Loving-Kindness Meditation Guided by Short Video Apps on Policemen’s Mindfulness, Public Service Motivation, Conflict Resolution Skills, and Communication Skills
papers.abstract: Police officers work in high-stress environments that demand emotional resilience, interpersonal skills, and effective communication. Occupational stress can negatively impact their motivation, conflict resolution abilities, and professional effectiveness. Loving-Kindness Meditation (LKM), a mindfulness-based intervention focused on cultivating compassion and empathy, has shown promise in enhancing prosocial attitudes and emotional regulation. With the rise of short video platforms, digital interventions like video-guided LKM may offer accessible mental health support for law enforcement. This study examines the effects of short video app-guided LKM on police officers’ mindfulness, public service motivation (PSM), conflict resolution skills (CRSs), and communication skills (CSSs). It aims to determine whether LKM can enhance these psychological and professional competencies. A randomized controlled trial (RCT) was conducted with 110 active-duty police officers from a metropolitan police department in China, with 92 completing the study. Participants were randomly assigned to either the LKM group (n = 46) or the waitlist control group (n = 46). The intervention consisted of a 6-week short video app-guided LKM program with daily 10 min meditation sessions. Pre- and post-intervention assessments were conducted using several validated scales: the Mindfulness Attention Awareness Scale (MAAS), the Public Service Motivation Scale (PSM), the Conflict Resolution Styles Inventory (CRSI), and the Communication Competence Scale (CCS). A 2 (Group: LKM vs. Control) × 2 (Time: Pre vs. Post) mixed-design MANOVA was conducted to analyze the effects. Statistical analyses revealed significant group-by-time interaction effects for PSM (F(4,177) = 21.793, p < 0.001, η2 = 0.108), CRS (F(4,177) = 20.920, p < 0.001, η2 = 0.104), and CSS (F(4,177) = 49.095, p < 0.001, η2 = 0.214), indicating improvements in these areas for LKM participants. However, no significant improvement was observed for mindfulness (F(4,177) = 2.850, p = 0.930, η2 = 0.016). Short video app-guided LKM improves public service motivation, conflict resolution skills, and communication skills among police officers but does not significantly enhance mindfulness. These findings suggest that brief, digitally delivered compassion-focused programs can be seamlessly incorporated into routine in-service training to strengthen officers’ prosocial motivation, de-escalation competence, and public-facing communication, thereby fostering more constructive police–community interactions.

papers.title: Frequent loving kindness meditation relates to lower anxiety in long term practitioners through higher self compassion and cognitive flexibility
papers.abstract: Little is known about the variables influencing the efficacy of mindfulness-based interventions among long-term practitioners. This study examined the association between Loving-Kindness Compassion Meditation (LKCM) practice and anxiety levels in 60 experienced meditators. We analyzed practice duration, frequency, self-compassion, and cognitive fusion. Results indicated no direct association between years of practice and anxiety. However, a moderated serial mediation model showed that the benefits are related to the frequency of practice. Weekly practice frequency moderated the relationship between years of meditation and self-compassion; furthermore, self-compassion was associated with lower cognitive fusion and this, in turn, with lower anxiety levels. Notably, high self-compassion was evident early in daily practitioners, whereas comparable levels were only observed in less frequent practitioners. These findings suggest that self-compassion and cognitive flexibility are critical components in prolonged meditation, highlighting the pivotal role of practice consistency over time. Supplementary Information The online version contains supplementary material available at 10.1038/s41598-026-46387-z.

papers.title: Effects of audio guided loving kindness meditation on psychological well being and laboratory stress responsiveness in healthy university students
papers.abstract: This study investigated the efficacy of a two-week online audio-guided loving-kindness meditation (LKM) program compared with mindfulness meditation (MF) and an active control (AC) group in a healthy university population. The study consisted of an overarching trial (N = 130), with a nested laboratory stress testing (N = 50). The full-sample subjective outcomes involved psychological distress, social approach and avoidance motivation, self-compassion, social connectedness, and positive and negative emotion. The nested laboratory testing examined the stress responsiveness to the socially evaluated cold pressor test, in terms of subjective stress, salivary cortisol, and blood pressure. All groups showed significant improvements in psychological distress, self-compassion, social connectedness, and negative emotion; however, no significant group differences were observed. For stress responsiveness, no significant differences were found across groups in average cortisol, blood pressure, or subjective stress levels. However, subsequent exploratory analyses yielded preliminary signals that the MF group, but not the LKM group, showed more attenuated cortisol activation and a higher completion rate on the cold pressor test than the AC group, which provides hypothesis-generating insights for future research. Overall, the findings did not support the relative superiority of LKM over MF and AC on both subjective indices and biological stress responsiveness.

Mechanistic insights toward dissociating therapeutic from psychedelic effects: bridging the gap between psychedelic research and mental health care
papers.abstract: Clinical trials investigating psychedelic compounds for depression and anxiety-related disorders are yielding promising preliminary results. Psychedelics produce profound alterations in brain function—such as suppression of the default mode network and thalamocortical dysregulation—leading to intense subjective experiences including ego dissolution and mystical-type states. While often described as meaningful or therapeutic, these effects can also be unpredictable or distressing. Because of these effects, which require labor-intensive, potentially cost-challenging preparation, administration, integration sessions, and exclude individuals with psychiatric vulnerabilities (e.g., bipolar disorder, borderline personality disorder, schizophrenia), questions remain about their real-world scalability. Consequently, there is growing interest in the possibility of dissociating the therapeutic benefits of psychedelics from their consciousness-altering effects. In this perspective, we examine emerging clinical and preclinical evidence investigating this scientifically timely and pressing question. Pharmacological strategies such as serotonin 2A receptor (5-HT2AR) antagonism and the development of “biased” psychedelic analogues or psychedelic-inspired compounds with reduced or null psychedelic potential may represent potential routes through which therapeutic efficacy may be retained even in the absence of psychedelic experiences. Current preclinical data suggest that downstream molecular and network-level mechanisms may mediate therapeutic effects independently of 5-HT2AR-driven subjective states. Whether these mechanisms can fully substitute for the experiential component of psychedelic therapy remains to be determined. Nonetheless, confirming this dissociation could mark a turning point in psychopharmacology, enabling the development of next-generation psychedelic-inspired treatments that may be more scalable, accessible, and appropriate for a broader range of psychiatric populations.

papers.title: Construct Overlap Between Two Widely Used Self-Report Measures of Dispositional Mindfulness: Evidence from Stress and Anxiety Control Outcomes.
papers.abstract: Researchers commonly conceptualise dispositional mindfulness as a multidimensional construct comprising attentional awareness, present-moment focus, and acceptance. However, widely used measures differ considerably in the dimensions they assess, raising questions regarding the extent to which they demonstrate construct overlap and can be considered interchangeable. The present study evaluated the psychometric functioning, construct overlap, and associations of the Mindful Attention Awareness Scale (MAAS) and the Freiburg Mindfulness Inventory (FMI) with stress and anxiety control outcomes. A community sample of 1,498 UK adults completed the MAAS, FMI, Perceived Stress Scale, and Anxiety Control Questionnaire. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), exploratory structural equation modelling (ESEM), Rasch analysis, and structural equation modelling (SEM) evaluated measurement properties and examined associations with stress and anxiety control outcomes. ESEM provided superior fit relative to CFA for multidimensional measures, while Rasch analyses indicated satisfactory measurement functioning across mindfulness measures. Contrary to expectations, despite satisfactory psychometric performance, the MAAS demonstrated near-zero correlations with the FMI total score and its Presence and Acceptance facets, indicating that these measures were essentially independent in this sample rather than showing substantial dimensional overlap. Structural models further revealed distinct patterns of association, with acceptance showing the strongest relationships with coping and emotion control, whereas mindfulness awareness displayed the strongest associations with threat control and stress control. Findings are consistent with multidimensional conceptualisations of mindfulness and demonstrate negligible convergence between the MAAS and FMI, indicating that researchers should not assume that these instruments are interchangeable. More broadly, the findings highlight the importance of empirically evaluating construct overlap when selecting scales intended to assess the same psychological construct.

papers.title: Effects and mechanisms of mindfulness acceptance commitment training on anxiety and cognitive flexibility in elite taekwondo athletes: A randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Competitive anxiety is a common challenge in elite taekwondo, where athletes must regulate pressure and rapidly adapt to changing tactical demands. This randomized controlled trial examined the effects of Mindfulness-Acceptance-Commitment (MAC) training on competitive anxiety and cognitive flexibility in elite taekwondo athletes. Eighty athletes were randomly assigned to an 8-week MAC group (n = 40) or an active Psychological Skills Training control group (PST; n = 40). Assessments were conducted at baseline (T0), immediately post-intervention (T1), and 3-month follow-up (T2) using self-report questionnaires and a computerized task-switching paradigm. Significant Group × Time interactions were found for cognitive anxiety, somatic anxiety, self-confidence, cognitive flexibility, and task-switching switch cost (all p < .01), indicating that changes differed between groups over time. The MAC group showed larger improvements in anxiety-related outcomes, self-confidence, and cognitive flexibility, with medium-to-large effects and the strongest effect for reduced switch cost (d = 1.67). Mediation analyses suggested that increased mindfulness and reduced experiential avoidance partially explained these changes. These findings provide preliminary evidence that MAC training may improve psychological regulation and adaptive cognitive functioning in elite taekwondo athletes, although further studies with larger samples and competition-based assessments are warranted.

Mindfulness-based stress reduction for sleep quality and emotional state in menopause-related insomnia symptoms.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study examined the efficacy and safety of mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) for menopause-related insomnia symptoms, with a focus on anxiety, depression, sleep quality, coping styles and quality of life. METHOD: Eighty-two patients with menopause-related insomnia symptoms were randomized into an experimental group ( RESULTS: Compared with routine care alone, the MBSR group achieved significantly larger decreases in Self-Rating Anxiety Scale and Self-Rating Depression Scale scores, lower Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores, more positive improvements in disease coping styles and more pronounced gains in several quality-of-life dimensions, particularly physical, psychological and social functioning ( CONCLUSION: This study confirms that 12-week MBSR is a safe and effective intervention for improving sleep quality, negative emotions, coping styles and quality of life in patients with menopause-related insomnia symptoms.

papers.title: Barriers to Complementary and Integrative Health Use Among Veterans on Long-Term Opioid Therapy.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Complementary and integrative health (CIH) therapies are increasingly promoted within the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) as nonpharmacologic approaches and adjuncts to long-term opioid therapy (LTOT) for chronic pain. However, uptake remains modest, and barriers to initiation and continuation are poorly understood. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of 126 Veterans with chronic pain on LTOT who had no CIH utilization documented in VHA electronic health records between July 1, 2017, and December 31, 2022. Participants were sampled from a national VHA cohort of over 280,000 Veterans. Respondents reported familiarity with nine CIH services-acupuncture, biofeedback, guided imagery, clinical hypnosis, therapeutic massage, meditation, tai chi/qi gong, yoga, and chiropractic care-as well as prior use and reasons for non-use or discontinuation. Barriers were summarized overall and stratified by age, sex, and race. RESULTS: Fewer than 10% of Veterans reported regular use of most modalities, with chiropractic care as the exception (23% regular use). Common reasons for non-use included lack of knowledge about eligibility, uncertainty about how to begin, and skepticism about effectiveness. Discontinuation was most often attributed to perceived ineffectiveness, cost, and logistical challenges. Younger Veterans more frequently reported not knowing they were eligible or how to start, while White Veterans more often cited doubts about effectiveness, and Black Veterans reported discomfort with particular modalities. Self-practice therapies (yoga and meditation) were more commonly practiced at home; whereas hands-on therapies (acupuncture, chiropractic care, and massage) were largely accessed in community settings where cost and logistics were prominent barriers. CONCLUSIONS: Substantial barriers remain to CIH service engagement among Veterans on LTOT, spanning awareness, logistics, and personal comfort. Targeted education, streamlined referrals, and strategies to manage early expectations may improve uptake and sustainment.
